messages.subject: Re: Interpretation of the STAR model
messages.body_plain:
As I understand it now (May 8) after reading the referred paper by Teräsvirta in the tsDyn- documentation, the STAR- algorithm performs a LM test of linearity and concludes that the model is linear. Then it fits a linear AR model instead.
This means that at this stage we cannot override the embedded LM- test when other tests shows the time series is nonlinear?.

On Tuesday, April 25, 2017 at 9:14:36 AM UTC+2, bjorn.gun...@tine.no wrote:
>
> I work as a dairy researcher and find the tsDyn package in R very useful. I used the Star- model to model a univariate time series.
>
> I get a message from R that the time series is linear, although several tests for linearity, e.g. the Tsay and Teräsvirta tests, reject this. My question is how to interpret the outcome of the model? Here it is:
>
>
>
> > modstar <- star(CH.train, mTh=c(0,1), control=list(maxit=3000),trace=TRUE)
>
> Testing linearity...   p-Value =  0.4524746
>
> The series is linear. Using linear model instead.
>
> > summary(modstar)
>
>
>
> Non linear autoregressive model
>
>
>
> AR model
>
> Coefficients:
>
>     const          phi.1      phi.2
>
> 85.386447  1.620855 -0.645020
>
>
>
> Fit:
>
> residuals variance = 15098,  AIC = 1623, MAPE = 2.436%
>
>
>
> Coefficient(s):
>
>         Estimate      Std. Error      t value     Pr(>|t|)
>
> const 85.386447   33.785045     2.5273    0.01244 *
>
> phi.1  1.620855      0.059109    27.4216    < 2e-16 ***
>
> phi.2 -0.645020      0.058783   -10.9729    < 2e-16 ***
>
>
>
> Does this mean that R fits a Star (AR1) model with varying weights on the two coefficients phi.1 and phi.2 to fit the dataset best possible?
>
> I get the messages that the series is linear for other time series as well, although the other tests suggest they are non- linear.
>
>
>
> Finally, what is the default Star model in the tsDyn package, the EStar (exponential) or the LStar (logistic)? I could not find any information on this in the documentation (tsDyn).
>
>
> I also tried to fit an LSTAR model but got error messages even though I tried to extend the grid search as described on page 36 in the documentation.
>
>
>
> Thanks in advance!
>
>
> Bjørn
messages.body_snippet: As I understand it now (May 8) after reading the referred paper by Teräsvirta in the tsDyn- documentation, the STAR- algorithm performs a LM test of linearity and concludes that the model is linear. T
